sentences.text:
Udit Narayan Sharma vs The State Of Madhya Pradesh on 8
September, 2025
 Neutral Citation No. 2025:Mphc-Jbp:42951
 1 
 In The High Court Of Madhya Pradesh

At Jabalpur
 Before
 Hon'Ble Shri Justice Devnarayan Mishra
 On The 8 th Of September, 2025
 Misc. Criminal Case No. 34914 of 2025
 Udit Narayan Sharma
 Versus
 The State Of Madhya Pradesh

Appearance:
 Mr. Siddharth Datt and Mr. Satya Prakash Mishra - Adv
 applicant.
 Mr. C.K.Mishra - Government Advocate for State.
 Order

This is the second application filed by the applicant under Section 483 o f Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita , 2023/ 439 of Code of Criminal Procedure for grant of regular bail relating to FIR/Crime No.1159 of 2023 registered at Police Station - Waidhan, District-Singrauli (M.P.) for the offence punishable under Sections 420, 467, 468, 471 and 120-B of the Indian Penal Code.
The applicant is in custody since 21.04.2025.
First bail application of the applicant was dismissed as withdrawn vide order dated 14.05.2025 passed in M.Cr.C. No.19174 of 2025.
2. Learned counsel for the applicant has submitted that the previous bail application of the applicant was dismissed as withdrawn as charge-sheet was not submitted.
Applicant is not required in the investigation as charge- sheet has been submitted on 17.07.2025.

It is alleged that the applicant has NEUTRAL CITATION NO. 2025:MPHC-JBP:42951 2 MCRC-34914-2025 mutated the land as per the order of Tahsildar and false allegations have been levelled against the applicant.
Other co-accused persons have already been granted the benefit of bail, hence, the applicant be released on bail.

3. Learned counsel for State has opposed the bail application and has submitted that there is active participation of the applicant in forging the documents and misappropriation of fund is proved,
hence, the applicant is not entitled to be released on bail.

4. Heard the parties and perused the case diary.

sentences.text: Looking to the facts and circumstance of the case coupled with the fact that no purpose would be served by keeping the applicant into custody as trial will take time to be concluded, this Court deems it appropriate to enlarge the applicant on bail, therefore, without commenting anything on the merit of the case, this bail application is allowed.

6. It is directed that applicant shall be released on bail on his furnishing personal bond in a sum of Rs.50,000/- (Rupees Fifty Thousand Only) with one surety in the like amount to the satisfaction of the trial Court concerned for his appearance before the said Court on all such dates as may be fixed by that Court in this regard during the pendency of trial.
7. It is further directed that the applicant shall comply with the provisions of Section 480(3) of BNSS.
8. Accordingly, Misc. Criminal Case stands disposed of.
